statement: Ensemble methods may improve recall on small datasets.
Mixed-precision ablations seem to reduce memory use at equal quality.
Late chunking might raise retrieval accuracy, though gains appear limited to long documents.
The index rebuild completes in one pass over the corpus.
Retrieval rerankers appear to help most on multi-hop questions.
The ablation suggests that dropout matters less at scale.
Speculative decoding could in principle halve latency without quality loss.
Cache-aware scheduling may cut tail latency, though the gains appear strongest under load.
